name: Hluboká Castle
label: Hluboká Castle
camera_source: Stand-here point set at the correction gate (own photo GPS 2026-11-17).
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap relation/444348: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Zámek Hluboká' (141 m across).
notes: Neo-Gothic Windsor-style castle of the Schwarzenbergs, the best-known sight in South Bohemia.

text.description: Hluboká Castle is a white, many-towered château that looks more English than Czech, and that is much of its charm. A Gothic castle stood here from the second half of the 13th century. It was later reworked in the Renaissance and Baroque styles. Its present look comes from a 19th-century rebuild in the romantic style of Windsor Castle, carried out between 1841 and 1871. The castle sits in an English-style park of roughly 1.9 square kilometres, so there is plenty of greenery to use as a frame. It is also one of the most visited castles in the Czech Republic, so expect other people with phones. Start with the default lens (1x) for the full front, with its battlements and pale stonework against the sky. Then try a gentle zoom for towers and rooflines. The ultra-wide lens (0.5x) helps if you want trees or a path in the foreground, but the castle will look smaller and a little stretched near the edges. Turn gridlines on and line up the towers with the vertical lines so they do not lean. Check the screen for people walking into the shot before you press the shutter.
text.geographic_location: Hluboká Castle stands in Hluboká nad Vltavou, in an English-style park.
text.directions_text: The spot is in Hluboká nad Vltavou. From there the castle is 134 m to the east, about 2 minutes on foot. The phone icon on the map is about 85 m west of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the whole castle. Use telephoto (2x-3x, or more if your phone has it) for towers, windows and roof details. Use ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a path, lawn or trees in the foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 85 m west of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face east.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and keep the towers upright against the vertical lines. Leave a little sky above the highest tower so the top is not cut off. For a more layered shot, include a tree branch or part of the park path at the edge of the frame, and keep the phone level so the horizon stays straight.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the castle's white walls to focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright and the stonework is turning too pale. Try panorama mode only if you can keep the phone steady and level while you turn.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Go on a dry day, with few people if you can. As you face east from where you stand, the sun may be behind the castle in the morning, so the afternoon is likely to give softer, more even light on the front.

text.access_note: The castle is open to the public, but entry to the interiors and some grounds may be ticketed or restricted, so check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Facing east from the stand-here point, the morning sun is likely to be behind the castle, so afternoon light may suit the front better.
The castle's walls are white or pale in colour.
The castle's front should fit in a 1x phone frame from about 134 m away.
There are usually other visitors taking photos around the castle.
Entry to interiors and some parts of the grounds may be ticketed or restricted.

name: Ohrada Zoo
label: Ohrada Zoo
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Zoo Hluboká' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Zoo Hluboká' (way/219935006): middle (576 m across).
pin_note: Position from the Wikipedia article 'Ohrada Zoo'.
notes: Zoo and hunting-lodge park in the woods south-west of the town.

text.description:
Ohrada Zoo, also called Zoo Hluboká, is the South Bohemian zoo in the town of Hluboká nad Vltavou. It opened in 1939 and keeps mainly animals from Europe and the Czech Republic, so the enclosures feel local rather than exotic. The zoo has a place in dog history too: its wolf Lejdy gave birth in 1983 to the last line of what became the Czechoslovakian Wolfdog breed.

For photographs, the best part is the pond side. The grounds sit on the south shore of the Munický rybník, so you can put calm water in the foreground and Hluboká chateau on the horizon beyond it. It is an easy way to get the zoo and the castle into one frame without any fuss.

Take a wide shot first to show the pond, the chateau and the shoreline together. Then move in for closer pictures of the animals. If you want a second view, the chateau itself looks back across the pond towards the Ohrada hunting lodge, with the zoo's grounds beside it. That is a distance shot of the lodge rather than of the zoo. Entry to both the zoo and the chateau may be ticketed, so check the official sites before you go.
text.geographic_location: Ohrada Zoo lies in the town of Hluboká nad Vltavou, on the south shore of the Munický rybník. Hluboká chateau can be seen across the pond.
text.directions_text: Start from the town centre of Hluboká nad Vltavou and head towards the Munický rybník, the pond on whose south shore the zoo sits. No public-transport stop is listed for this spot, so plan to cover the last stretch on foot. Once you are there, look towards the pond side of the zoo. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) for the pond, the sky and the chateau together. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural view. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to bring the chateau closer or to photograph animals from a distance.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject (pond side of the zoo, on the south shore of the Munický rybník). The zoo's pond-side grounds with the water in the foreground and Hluboká chateau rising on the horizon across the pond. Look in that direction towards the zoo's pond-side grounds on the south shore of the Munický rybník, with the water in the foreground and Hluboká chateau on the horizon across the pond.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and put the water's edge on the lower line, with the chateau near one of the upper crossing points. Keep a little shoreline or greenery at the edge of the frame so the picture has depth. For an alternative view, the chateau looks back across the pond towards the Ohrada hunting lodge and the zoo's grounds.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the chateau to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the sky keeps its colour. For animals, tap on the eye and wait for the focus to settle before pressing the shutter. Portrait mode can suit animals that stay still and are close enough.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: There is no single best time, but softer morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters the water and the chateau. Check the zoo's opening hours before you plan your visit.

text.access_note: The zoo is an attraction with its own grounds, and the chateau is a paid attraction, so check the official sites before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Softer morning or late-afternoon light is generally more flattering for photographs of water and buildings.
Portrait mode on a phone can work for animals that are close and still.
Entry to the zoo may be ticketed.

name: Waldemar statue
label: Waldemar Statue
pin_note: Position from OSM N13970924760 (Waldemar): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Sculpture by Jaroslav Róna in the lower castle garden.

text.description:
The Waldemar statue is a statue in Hluboká nad Vltavou and the third spot on this map.

A statue photographs best when it has some space around it. Walking round it will show you which side has the cleanest background. Watch for signs, parked cars, bins and people in the background, and step a metre or two sideways to lose them.

On the default lens (1x), stand a few steps back and keep the phone upright so the whole figure and its base fit in. Switch gridlines on to keep the statue straight. If the sky behind is bright, tap on the statue to focus and pull the exposure slider down a little so the figure doesn't turn into a dark shape. Use the telephoto lens for details such as the face or the base. Portrait mode can also soften a busy background.

This text gives no history, dates or size for the statue. Look for any information board nearby if you want the background.
text.geographic_location: The Waldemar statue is in Hluboká nad Vltavou, about 154 metres west of the stand-here point on the map.
text.directions_text: No public transport stops are listed near this spot. Follow the map to the statue. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the statue and its surroundings. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for details, and the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you can stand close and want to include a lot of the setting.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Take a first wide shot as you approach, then move closer.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on gridlines and keep the statue upright and level. Leave a little space above the head and around the base. Step sideways to keep poles, signs and people out of the background. Take one wide picture and one close one.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the statue to focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly if the sky is bright, so the figure keeps its detail. Try portrait mode for a close shot if the background is busy.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light usually flatters statues better than harsh midday sun. Overcast days also work well for even light.

text.access_note: Access rules for this spot are not known to us, so check the official site before you go.
